back_blocks.md: A **partition coefficient** (*K*<sub>pc</sub>) is the ratio of the concentration of a solute in an organic solvent to its concentration in water (or vice versa), at equilibrium and at a specified temperature.

cards.back_md: A **partition coefficient** (*K*<sub>pc</sub>) is the ratio of the concentration of a solute in an organic solvent to its concentration in water (or vice versa), at equilibrium and at a specified temperature.

front_blocks.md: State the equilibrium expression for the partition coefficient of methylamine (CH<sub>3</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>) distributed between an organic solvent and water.

front_blocks.md: When *K*<sub>pc</sub> is greater than 1, the solute is more soluble in the organic solvent than in water.

back_blocks.md: *K*<sub>pc</sub> > 1 means [solute in organic] > [solute in water], so the solute has a higher solubility in the organic solvent.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

When *K*<sub>pc</sub> is greater than 1, the solute is more soluble in the organic solvent than in water.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

*K*<sub>pc</sub> > 1 means [solute in organic] > [solute in water], so the solute has a higher solubility in the organic solvent.

front_blocks.md: The partition coefficient depends on the **..........**  of the solute in each solvent, which is determined by the strength of **..........**  forces between solute and solvent molecules.

back_blocks.md: The partition coefficient depends on the **solubility** of the solute in each solvent, which is determined by the strength of **intermolecular** forces between solute and solvent molecules.

cards.front_md: The partition coefficient depends on the **..........**  of the solute in each solvent, which is determined by the strength of **..........**  forces between solute and solvent molecules.
cards.back_md: The partition coefficient depends on the **solubility** of the solute in each solvent, which is determined by the strength of **intermolecular** forces between solute and solvent molecules.

front_blocks.md: Explain why ammonia has a lower partition coefficient (organic / water) than expected from its molecular mass alone.

back_blocks.md: Ammonia and water are both polar and form **hydrogen bonds** with each other. Ammonia forms only weaker permanent dipole-induced dipole interactions with non-polar organic solvents. The stronger hydrogen bonding makes ammonia more soluble in water, lowering *K*<sub>pc</sub>.

cards.front_md: Explain why ammonia has a lower partition coefficient (organic / water) than expected from its molecular mass alone.
cards.back_md: Ammonia and water are both polar and form **hydrogen bonds** with each other. Ammonia forms only weaker permanent dipole-induced dipole interactions with non-polar organic solvents. The stronger hydrogen bonding makes ammonia more soluble in water, lowering *K*<sub>pc</sub>.

front_blocks.md: The partition coefficient changes with temperature.

back_blocks.md: *K*<sub>pc</sub> depends on the solubilities of the solute in each solvent, which are temperature-dependent. A change in temperature alters the equilibrium position and therefore the value of *K*<sub>pc</sub>.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The partition coefficient changes with temperature.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

*K*<sub>pc</sub> depends on the solubilities of the solute in each solvent, which are temperature-dependent. A change in temperature alters the equilibrium position and therefore the value of *K*<sub>pc</sub>.

front_blocks.md: In a partition coefficient calculation using titration, why is only part of the aqueous layer titrated rather than all of it?

back_blocks.md: A measured **aliquot** (e.g. 50.0 cm<sup>3</sup>) is titrated for precision and practicality. The moles found in that aliquot are then **scaled up** proportionally to find the total moles of solute in the full aqueous layer.

back_blocks.md: **Immiscible solvents** are two liquids that do not mix and form two distinct layers when combined, such as water and an organic solvent like hexane. A solute can distribute between both layers, establishing a partition equilibrium.

cards.back_md: **Immiscible solvents** are two liquids that do not mix and form two distinct layers when combined, such as water and an organic solvent like hexane. A solute can distribute between both layers, establishing a partition equilibrium.

front_blocks.md: If *K*<sub>pc</sub> (organic / water) < 1, the solute is more soluble in **..........**  . If *K*<sub>pc</sub> > 1, it is more soluble in **..........**  .

back_blocks.md: If *K*<sub>pc</sub> (organic / water) < 1, the solute is more soluble in **water**. If *K*<sub>pc</sub> > 1, it is more soluble in **the organic solvent**.
